---
title: Configuration
---

`biblint.toml` answers three questions:

1. Which BibTeX files belong to this project?
2. Which lint rules should run?
3. How should matching files be formatted?

Keep the file in version control, usually at the repository root.
The command line chooses the operation (`check` or `format`); the configuration chooses the policy shared by both commands.

## Find the right files

Without `--config`, biblint searches upward from the first input path until it finds `biblint.toml`.
An explicitly supplied config path takes precedence.
This means a command launched from a subdirectory still uses the repository policy.

For a directory input, biblint visits `.bib` files recursively.
`include` and `exclude` patterns then decide which files are used:

```toml
include = ["**/*.bib"]
exclude = ["vendor/**", "generated/**"]
default-exclude = true
```

An explicit file does not need a `.bib` extension, although it is still subject to the configured include and exclude patterns.
Recursive scans skip `.git/**` and `target/**` when `default-exclude` is `true`.

## Select rules

The default rule set is a useful starting point.
Use `extend-select` to add opt-in rules while keeping the defaults, or use `select` when you want to define the complete set yourself.
`ignore` always wins over either selection method.

```toml
[lint]
# Add checks without removing the defaults.
extend-select = ["duplicate_doi", "key_format"]

# Replace the defaults entirely when a small, explicit set is preferable.
# select = ["syntax_error", "duplicate_key"]

# Disable a selected rule, including one added above.
# ignore = ["key_format"]
```

Use `all` as a wildcard.
Per-file ignores use the same rule names and are useful for generated or legacy data:

```toml
[lint.per-file-ignores]
"generated/**" = ["formatting", "unsupported_construct"]
```

Formatting is not part of `check` by default because it is a rewrite rather than a content diagnostic.
Use `biblint check --format` for a one-off formatting check, select `formatting` in the config, or use `biblint format --check` when formatting is the only gate you need.

## A practical starter file

This profile scans project bibliographies, ignores vendored/generated files, adds duplicate DOI/citation and citekey checks, and sorts the output predictably:

```toml
include = ["**/*.bib"]
exclude = ["vendor/**", "generated/**"]
default-exclude = true

[lint]
extend-select = ["duplicate_doi", "duplicate_citation", "key_format"]

[lint.key-format]
style = "better-bibtex"

[format]
indent = 2
align = false
lowercase = true
sort = ["key"]
sort-fields = ["title", "author", "year"]
```

The key-format section enables the Better BibTeX-compatible style for checking existing keys.
It does not rename them; see [Citekey generation](key-generation.md) when you want to generate and apply new keys.

## Validate a configuration

Unknown settings, rule names, invalid globs, and invalid citekey formulas are rejected when the configuration loads.
Settings omitted from the file use their defaults, so start small and add only the policy your project needs.
